count-up.why: Each call recurses first and prints afterwards, so the deepest call (n = 1) prints first as the calls unwind.

naive-fibonacci.why: Each call makes two more, so the call tree roughly doubles at every level, n levels deep: exponential. (It's more precisely about 1.618ⁿ, which is still exponential.) Memoisation brings it down to O(n).

recursive-sum-space.why: The method uses no extra arrays, but the recursion goes n calls deep before any call returns, and each frame lives on the call stack at once.

binary-search-space.why: Each call halves the range, so the recursion is at most about log₂ n calls deep. An iterative version needs only O(1).

merge-sort.why: There are about log₂ n levels of halving, and the merges on each level touch all n elements once.

all-subsets.why: This is an output-sensitive bound: the output itself has 2ⁿ entries (and up to n items each), so producing it costs at least that much, however clever the algorithm.

amortized-append.why: Most adds are O(1). When the backing array is full it grows by a constant factor and copies everything, but those copies add up to less than a constant times n overall, so each add is O(1) amortized.

aux-copy.why: Auxiliary space counts extra memory the algorithm allocates beyond its input. A full copy is n extra slots, whatever the running time.
